stem: Though the researcher described the archive as incomplete, her conclusions were not [blank]; each was carefully limited to the documents that had survived.
explanation: The second clause says the conclusions were carefully limited, so they were not reckless. Tentative is tempting but would fit the careful limitation rather than contrast with it.

stem: The auditor's report was unusually [blank], cataloging even minor discrepancies that earlier reviews had dismissed as immaterial.
explanation: The cataloging of even minor discrepancies points to unusually careful attention to detail. Fastidious and meticulous produce similar completed meanings.

passage: A school district adopted an early-warning system that flags students as academically at risk when their attendance, grades, and disciplinary records cross certain thresholds. Administrators reported that flagged students who received counseling were more likely to pass their courses than flagged students who did not. On this basis, they argued that expanding the system would by itself substantially increase graduation rates. Some teachers, however, noted that counselors often selected students whose families had already requested help, and that the system did not identify students whose grades declined abruptly after the reporting period ended.
stem: Which of the following, if true, most weakens the administrators' argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many students who were flagged had poor attendance before their grades began to fall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The counseling program was most effective for students whose families had independently sought academic support.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The district used the same thresholds in middle schools and high schools.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several neighboring districts use early-warning systems with more categories.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teachers received training on how to interpret the warning reports.

explanation: The argument treats the system expansion itself as the likely cause of better outcomes. Choice B suggests selection bias: counseling success may reflect family initiative rather than the warning system alone.
